explanation: The ADR describes the decision to create and implement a specific architectural pattern involving components such as connectors, containers, and wrapped components to manage state and views in a Polymer project. This is about creating and selecting architectural elements (containers, connectors, components) that will exist in the system design and implementation. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general system properties, or governing development processes, but about defining structural and behavioral elements of the system.

The ADR decides to create and use specific software elements (Ansible roles and playbooks) as part of the system's deployment and provisioning architecture. This is about selecting and creating architectural elements that will exist in the system to be built. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing the development process itself. Although Ansible is a tool for deployment, here it is part of the system's provisioning architecture, thus an Existence decision.

The ADR defines rules and constraints about versioning and release mechanisms, which are enduring qualities and constraints of the system's build and release process. It does not create or forbid specific architectural elements (Existence or Ban), nor does it govern the development process or organizational aspects (Executive). Instead, it sets properties about how versions and builds are managed and labeled, which is a system property.

The ADR sets a general rule about how configuration keys should be structured and how default values should be handled in the system. It defines a quality or constraint on configuration management rather than creating or forbidding specific architectural elements or dictating development processes.

The ADR primarily addresses the creation and management of release candidate (rc) artifacts in the build and release process, which are elements of the software system's artifact repository. The decision involves whether and how these rc artifacts exist or are created automatically when cutting release branches, which is a structural/behavioral element of the system's artifact management. This fits the Existence category as it concerns the creation and presence of specific artifacts in the system. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting general system properties or constraints (Property), nor about development process or organizational decisions unrelated to the system elements themselves (Executive). Although the decision touches on process aspects, the core subject is the existence and creation of rc artifacts, which are part of the system's architecture.

The ADR focuses on the decision to implement a new version (v2) of the Message Driven Content Tracker as part of the system architecture, which involves creating and selecting architectural elements such as the new Search Services architecture and changes in Content Repository. This is a clear Existence decision as it declares that these elements will exist in the system design and implementation. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban), setting general system properties or constraints (Property), or about development process or organizational aspects (Executive).

The ADR primarily decides to create and use Kubernetes secret objects within the system deployment to manage sensitive information. This is a decision about the existence of a specific architectural element (Kubernetes secrets) in the system design. Although it also discusses security practices and integration with external providers, the core decision is about the inclusion of these secret objects as part of the system architecture. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing development processes, so Ban/Non-Existence, Property, and Executive categories are less appropriate.

The ADR primarily decides on the existence and setup of configuration elements within the application architecture, specifically how configuration data (environment variables or static JSON) will be injected and used at runtime. This is about creating or selecting a structural element (configuration mechanism) that will exist in the system design. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting a general quality or constraint (Property), nor about development process or organizational decisions (Executive). Although it touches on deployment and infrastructure, the core decision is about the presence and method of configuration elements in the system, which is an Existence decision.

The ADR primarily decides on the existence of a specific architectural element: a web application with offline capabilities (a Progressive Web App) as the platform for the system. This is a structural decision about what kind of application will be built and deployed. Although there is some discussion about development feasibility and resource constraints, the core decision is about selecting the type of application to exist in the system. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting general system properties or constraints (Property), nor about development process or organizational aspects (Executive).

The ADR decides to include a specific architectural element, the 'gorilla/mux' router, as part of the system design to handle routing. This is a clear decision about creating/selecting a software element for the system, which fits the Existence category. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), setting general system properties or constraints (Property), or about development process or organizational context (Executive).

The ADR primarily defines rules, constraints, and quality requirements for audit logging, such as what data can be logged, what must be masked or encrypted, retention policies, and compliance standards. It does not decide on creating or selecting specific architectural elements (Existence), forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), or dictate development processes or organizational policies (Executive). Instead, it sets enduring properties and constraints on the system's logging behavior and data handling, fitting the Property category.

The ADR describes the decision to create and use a specific structural element in the UI architecture: wrapping <input> and <textarea> elements in a div.wrapper and applying styles to this wrapper. This is a decision about the existence of a design element in the system's structure, not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or development processes. Therefore, it fits the Existence category.

The ADR primarily decides which programming languages will be used for new service development, effectively selecting architectural elements (languages) that will exist in the system. This is a classic Existence decision as it defines what elements will be part of the system's implementation. Although it touches on team skills and procurement, these are secondary considerations supporting the main decision about the system's composition. It is not a Property decision because it does not set a quality or constraint on behavior or structure, but rather selects concrete elements. It is not Executive because it governs what is built, not how the development process is managed overall. It is not Ban/Non-Existence because it does not forbid languages outright but restricts to a set of allowed languages with exceptions requiring justification.

The ADR defines the creation and existence of specific data entities (Tasks, Submissions, Entries, Files) as part of the system's data structure. This is a structural decision about what elements will exist in the system design and implementation. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing development processes, so Ban/Non-Existence, Property, and Executive categories are not appropriate.

The ADR decides to create a new architectural element: a CSV data export component within the API application that generates and stores finance data exports. This is a structural decision about adding a specific element to the system to fulfill a functional need. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban), setting general system properties or constraints (Property), or about development process or organizational decisions (Executive). Therefore, it fits best as an Existence decision.

The ADR explicitly decides not to implement an 'extensions' mechanism in the API at this time, effectively forbidding the existence of such a mechanism in the current design. This is a decision to exclude a potential architectural element (the extensions mechanism) rather than to create or select one, so it fits the Ban/Non-Existence category. It is not about setting a property or quality of the system, nor about development process or organizational decisions, so Property and Executive categories are discarded. It is also not an Existence decision because it does not create or select an architectural element; rather, it forbids one.

The ADR decides to use DotEnv as a tool to load environment variables into the system. This is a decision about creating/choosing a specific architectural element (a library/component) that will exist in the system to manage environment variables. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing the development process. Although it mentions testing support, the core decision is about the existence of DotEnv as part of the system's runtime environment management.

The decision mandates the creation and integration of a new system element: the automated integration of the Database for Qualified Teachers (DQT) service into the claim service for validating teacher identity and qualifications. This is a clear architectural existence decision about adding a new component and interaction (API integration) to the system. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing development processes, but about what elements will exist in the system design and implementation.

The ADR primarily decides on the creation and selection of architectural elements such as an API Gateway, REST Proxy, and Event Backbone for integrating data sources. These are concrete architectural elements that will exist in the system design and implementation. Although there are some process-related aspects (e.g., dedicated teams), the core decision is about what components will be part of the system to enable integration, which aligns with the Existence category. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), setting general system properties or constraints (Property), or governing development processes or organizational aspects (Executive).

The decision is about choosing a specific type of identifier (non-integer IDs using Rails' has_secure_token) for trainee entities in the system. This directly affects the structural element of the system (the identifier used in URLs and data records), which is an architectural element. It is not about forbidding an element, setting a general property, or about the development process, but about the existence and selection of a system element (the ID type).

The decision is about selecting a specific software element, Skylight, to be used for performance monitoring in the system. This is a clear example of an Existence decision because it declares that Skylight will exist as part of the system's architecture to fulfill a monitoring function. It is not about forbidding an element, setting a general property, or governing the development process, but about choosing a component to be included in the system design.

The ADR primarily decides on the existence and configuration of deployment environments (staging and production) for the system after migration to GOV.UK PaaS. It specifies which environments will exist and be maintained as part of the system's architecture. This is a structural decision about the system's runtime elements. It is not about forbidding environments (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting general system properties or qualities, nor about development process or organizational policies (Executive). Although it touches on development practices (e.g., developers using local environments), the core decision is about which environments exist as part of the system deployment architecture.

The decision sets a general guiding principle or quality attribute for the system development: prioritize simplicity and readability over premature optimization, and only optimize when real performance issues are confirmed. It is a rule about system behavior and quality rather than about creating or forbidding specific elements or about the development process itself.

The decision sets a general rule about the system's behavior: the inverse relationship process should not update the sample's update date. This is a quality or constraint on system behavior rather than creating or forbidding an element, or governing the development process.

The decision sets a general rule about how to represent types in schema.org data, specifying that '@type' or rdf:type should be used for typing resources outside the core vocabulary. This is a design rule or constraint about data semantics and querying, rather than creating or banning an architectural element or dictating development process. It governs a quality or property of the data representation.

The decision defines a general, enduring quality or constraint on the system: booleans must be represented as strings '0' or '1' in the KeySet for type=boolean, with specific rules about defaults and error handling. This is a cross-cutting design rule about data representation and validation, not about creating or forbidding elements, nor about development process.

The decision explicitly states the removal of certain functions from the API, which means these elements will no longer exist in the design or implementation. This fits the Ban/Non-Existence category as it forbids the existence of these functions. It is not about creating or selecting elements (Existence), nor about setting general properties or constraints (Property), nor about development process or organizational decisions (Executive).

The ADR explicitly declares that multiple file backends for writing are not supported, effectively forbidding the existence of writable multiple file backends in the system design. This is a clear decision to ban a certain architectural element. It is not about creating or selecting an element (Existence), nor about setting a general property or quality (Property), nor about development process or organizational aspects (Executive).

The decision focuses on the structural element of the system, specifically the storage of key names within the 'struct _Key'. It decides to only store the unescaped key name in the core data structure, which is a clear architectural element of the system. This is an Existence decision because it defines what elements (unescaped key name) will exist in the system's design and implementation. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting a general quality or constraint (Property), nor about development process or organizational aspects (Executive).

The decision is about naming and branding the project to set clear boundaries and expectations about its scope and purpose. It establishes a general, enduring quality or constraint on how the project is perceived and what features it should include, rather than creating or forbidding specific architectural elements or dictating development processes.

The decision mandates the creation of a new architectural element: an HTTP API as a single access point to the FlowMachine library. This is a structural decision introducing a new component in the system architecture to replace direct library access. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing development processes, but about creating a specific element in the system design.

The decision is about creating the basis of the project structure by using create-react-app and npm eject, which means selecting and creating specific architectural elements (project scaffold, configuration) that will exist in the system. This is a clear Existence decision as it defines what elements will be part of the system to be built. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban), setting general system properties or constraints (Property), or about the development process or organizational context (Executive).

The ADR describes the decision to document architectural decisions as part of the versioning system and development process. It governs how the team works and manages architectural knowledge rather than specifying any architectural element or quality of the system itself. Therefore, it is an Executive decision related to the development process and organizational practice.

The decision defines the existence and structure of a new architectural element in the system: the Continuous Inpatient Spell (CIPS) as a grouping of inpatient spells with specific rules and derived variables. It also creates a new CIPS table representing these elements. This is a structural decision about what elements will exist in the system design and implementation. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing development processes, so Ban/Non-Existence, Property, and Executive categories are discarded.

The decision specifies the choice of a logging mechanism (logging to stdout/stderr with specific formatting) as part of the system's design. This is about selecting a concrete architectural element (logging output method) that will exist in the system. It is not about forbidding an element, setting a general property, or governing the development process, so Ban/Non-Existence, Property, and Executive categories are not appropriate.

The decision declares that environment variables will exist as a configuration element in the system design. It specifies the use of environment variables as a mechanism to configure applications, which is a structural and behavioral element of the system. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general system properties, or about development process or organizational aspects, so Ban/Non-Existence, Property, and Executive categories are less appropriate.

The decision specifies the use of ETags and a mechanism involving HTTP headers (ETag and If-Match) to handle eventual consistency in the system. This introduces specific architectural elements (ETag headers, ProjectionState updates, and API response behaviors) that will exist in the system design and implementation to manage resource state consistency. It is about creating and selecting architectural elements and behaviors in the system, not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing development processes.

The decision defines the existence and use of specific elements in the system: temporary and permanent identifiers for road network entities. It specifies how these identifiers are created, assigned, and managed as part of the system's design. This is about creating and managing architectural elements (identifiers) that exist in the system, thus fitting the Existence category. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about general system properties or constraints (Property), nor about development process or organizational decisions (Executive).

The decision specifies that certain Docker images will exist pre-installed on the device by shipping them in a data volume. This is about creating and including specific software elements (Docker images) in the system design. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general system properties, or governing development processes, but about the existence of these images as part of the system's runtime environment.

The ADR decides to include a specific architectural element in the system design: the use of a regular expression-based approach for splitting multiple-sentence titles. This is a structural decision about how the system will process titles, thus it is about creating/selecting a software element or behavior in the system. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting a general quality or constraint (Property), nor about development process or organizational aspects (Executive).

The decision focuses on whether the 'study' should remain a pure Data Transfer Object (DTO) or contain direct object instances. This is about setting a design rule or constraint on the structure and behavior of the system's data representation, rather than creating or forbidding a specific architectural element or dictating a development process. It establishes a property regarding how data is modeled and transformed, which is a general, enduring quality of the system design.

The decision is about choosing C++ as the programming language to interface with the ftduino, which is a software element of the system to be built. This is a structural decision about the technology and language used in the system's implementation, thus it fits the Existence category. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting general system properties or constraints (Property), nor about development process or organizational aspects (Executive).

The ADR proposes a fundamental redesign of the core data API and data format used in the system, specifically introducing a new 'Data' class and changing the pipeline step interfaces to use this new data representation. This is a decision about creating and selecting new architectural elements (the Data class, new pipeline step APIs, new serialization formats) that will exist in the system design and implementation. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties or constraints, or about development process or organizational decisions. Therefore, it fits best in the Existence category.

The decision is about creating a new architectural element: an abstracted resident data source within the application. This is a structural decision to include a component (the resident store) in the system design, which will later be replaced or integrated with an external data source. It is not about forbidding elements, setting system-wide properties, or governing development processes, but about the existence of a software element in the architecture.

The ADR decides to use specific architectural elements, namely AWS SNS and SQS services, to implement an event-driven architecture for microservices communication. This is a decision about creating and selecting components (message brokers) that will exist in the system design to enable asynchronous messaging and decoupling. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing development processes.

The decision is about adopting ESLint as a tool to enforce code style and consistency during development. ESLint is used as part of the development process (linting and testing), not as a runtime component of the system. Therefore, this decision governs how the team works rather than what is built in the system, making it an Executive decision.

The decision is about re-implementing JavaScript features from the govuk-frontend library internally within this library, effectively creating new software elements (idiomatic React implementations) as part of the system. This is a clear Existence decision because it involves creating architectural elements (JavaScript modules) that will exist in the system. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor is it primarily about setting general system properties or constraints (Property). It also does not govern the development process or organizational aspects (Executive).

The decision is about selecting a specific architectural element (Postgres Search) to implement the search functionality within the system. This is a clear example of an Existence decision because it creates or chooses a software element that will exist in the system. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing the development process.

The decision is about selecting and using a specific architectural element (the existing OAI-PMH/ORE tool and custom scripts) as part of the system's ingest process. This directly relates to what elements will exist in the system to handle data ingestion. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general system properties, or governing development processes, but about choosing components that will be part of the running system.

The decision is about selecting AWS Lambda as the compute model for the data processing pipeline, which is a specific architectural element of the system to be built. This clearly fits the Existence category as it declares that a particular element (AWS Lambda functions) will exist in the system design and implementation. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general system properties, or governing the development process, so Ban/Non-Existence, Property, and Executive categories are not appropriate.

The decision mandates the use of Docker containers for all services and applications, which means creating and selecting a specific architectural element (Docker containers) as part of the system design and implementation. This is a structural decision about the elements that will exist in the system. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing the development process itself, but about what elements will be part of the system architecture.

The decision is about selecting Kubernetes as the container orchestration platform, which is a specific architectural element that will exist in the system design. It directly affects the system's runtime structure and behavior by managing containers across servers. This fits the Existence category as it declares the presence of a key system component. It is not about forbidding an element (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting a general quality or constraint (Property), nor about the development process or organizational aspects (Executive). Although the team needs to learn Kubernetes, that is a consequence, not the core decision, so it does not make this an Executive decision.

The decision is about selecting a specific software element, the Prometheus Operator Helm Chart, to be part of the system's deployment architecture. This is a clear example of an Existence decision because it determines which component will exist in the system. It is not about forbidding elements, setting system-wide properties, or governing the development process, so other categories are discarded.

The decision sets a general, enduring quality or constraint on the system: all services must have default configuration values. It is not about creating or forbidding a specific architectural element (Existence or Ban/Non-Existence), nor about the development process or organizational aspects (Executive). Instead, it defines a design rule or property that applies across services regarding configuration behavior.

The ADR's core decision is to replace the existing relational database with a JSON document database as the persistence mechanism for the system. This is a clear architectural decision about the existence and selection of a key software element (the database technology) that will be part of the running system. It is about what to build and how the system will store and manage data, which fits the Existence category. It is not about forbidding an element (Ban/Non-Existence), nor is it primarily about setting a general quality or constraint (Property), nor about development process or organizational context (Executive). Although there are process and organizational implications, the primary focus is on the architectural element to be created and used in the system.

The ADR primarily decides on the existence and structure of specific cookies and their properties in the system design, which are architectural elements of the system. It defines what cookies (elements) will exist, what properties they will hold, and how they interact with the session and user preferences. This is a clear Existence decision as it creates and selects architectural elements (cookies) that are part of the running system. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor is it a general quality or constraint (Property), nor about development process or organizational context (Executive).

The decision declares that specific testing frameworks (Jest and Cypress) will be used in the system, which means these tools become part of the system's design and implementation for testing purposes. This is about creating/selecting elements (testing frameworks) that exist in the system. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing the development process itself, but about choosing concrete elements to be part of the system's testing architecture.

The ADR decides to include React Router as a client-side routing element in the system and to generate HTML files for each pixel art entry to support routing and link previews. This is about creating and selecting architectural elements (React Router routes, generated HTML files) that will exist in the system design and implementation. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general system properties, or governing development processes.

The ADR decides on the structure and type of the error object that will exist in the system design and implementation. It defines how errors are represented and propagated, specifically by introducing a new error class with additional properties (e.g., originalError and rootError). This is about creating and selecting a specific architectural element (error object) in the system, which fits the Existence category. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting general system properties or constraints (Property), nor about development process or organizational decisions (Executive).

The ADR defines naming conventions and rules for generated APIs, operations, properties, and query parameters, which are enduring qualities or constraints on the system's naming behavior. It does not create or forbid specific architectural elements (Existence or Ban), nor does it govern the development process (Executive). Instead, it sets rules about naming properties and parameters, which is a system property.

The ADR primarily decides to create new architectural elements in the system design: form field variations and form groups as new elements with attributes like 'version' and 'groupid'. These are structural elements of the form system that will exist in the implementation. Although there are some considerations about data structure and UI development, the core decision is about creating and organizing new form field and group elements, which fits the Existence category. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting general system properties or constraints (Property), nor about development process or organizational decisions (Executive).

The decision sets general guidelines and rules for writing documentation for components, focusing on style, language, and content constraints. It does not create or forbid any architectural elements, nor does it dictate development processes. Instead, it establishes enduring qualities and constraints on documentation, which is a cross-cutting concern, fitting the Property category.

The decision is about selecting specific software elements (Redis and Bull) to be part of the system architecture for handling background tasks. This is a structural/behavioral decision about what components exist in the system to fulfill a functional need (background processing). It is not about forbidding elements, setting general system properties, or governing development processes.

The ADR decides to create and organize specific architectural elements in the system: separate source directories for integration and unit tests. This is a structural decision about the organization of test artifacts in the codebase, which fits the Existence category as it defines elements that will exist in the system design. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting general system properties or qualities (Property), nor about development process or organizational rules (Executive).

The decision explicitly declares that node type definitions will not be supported in the TOSCA service template, effectively forbidding the existence of this element in the design. This matches the Ban/Non-Existence category, which is about ruling out certain elements. It is not about creating or selecting an element (Existence), nor about setting a general property or quality (Property), nor about development process or organizational aspects (Executive).

The ADR primarily decides on the architectural approach to handle non-CRUD operations in the REST API, specifically selecting how to represent and implement these operations as part of the system's API design. This involves creating or choosing specific architectural elements such as custom endpoints or resource representations (e.g., controller archetype with custom verbs in URLs). This is a clear Existence decision because it defines what elements (custom operations/endpoints) will exist in the system's architecture. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting general system properties or constraints (Property), nor about development process or organizational decisions (Executive). Although there is some discussion about process and conventions, the core decision is about the existence and design of API elements to support non-CRUD operations.

The decision is about injecting variables (AB tests, config, global values) into presenters via their constructors, which means creating or modifying the structure of the system elements (presenters) to include these dependencies. This is a structural decision about the design of the system components, thus an Existence decision. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting general system properties or constraints (Property), nor about development process or organizational aspects (Executive).

The decision is about adopting a specific software element, the 'govuk_design_system_formbuilder', to be used in the system for building forms compliant with the GOV.UK Design System. This is a clear creation/selection of an architectural element (a form builder component) that will exist in the system. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing the development process, but about choosing a concrete component to be part of the system's architecture.

The ADR decides to include a specific architectural element, the 'data-migrate' gem, as part of the system to handle data migrations separately from schema migrations. This is a decision about creating and selecting a software element that will exist in the system's design and implementation. It also defines a process step (rake data:migrate) as part of deployment, but this is tied to the existence and operation of the data migration element within the system, not just the development process. Therefore, it fits best as an Existence decision. It is not a Property decision because it does not set a general quality or constraint; it is not a Ban/Non-Existence decision because it does not forbid elements; and it is not an Executive decision because it is about what is built and included in the system, not about how the team works or the development methodology.

The decision sets a general rule or pattern for how common tasks are handled in the project (using the 'Scripts to Rule Them All' pattern). It is not about creating a specific architectural element (Existence), forbidding an element (Ban/Non-Existence), or about the development process or organizational aspects (Executive). Instead, it establishes a cross-cutting design guideline or quality about task automation and documentation, which fits the Property category.

The decision explicitly declares that HATEOAS links will be removed from all entities, meaning these elements will no longer exist in the design or implementation. This fits the Ban/Non-Existence category as it forbids the presence of a specific architectural element. It is not about creating or selecting an element (Existence), nor about setting a general quality or constraint (Property), nor about development process or organizational context (Executive).

The ADR decides on the method to transfer and verify JSON data integrity by choosing to send a SHA256 hash of Base64Url encoded JSON. This decision creates a specific architectural element or artifact (the verification token and its encoding/decoding process) that will exist in the system design and implementation. It is about what is built to ensure data integrity, not about process or organizational aspects, nor forbidding elements or setting general properties.

The ADR decides to use 'nix' as the dependency management tool for the system, which is a specific architectural element that will exist in the system design and implementation. This is a clear selection of a software element that becomes part of the system's build and runtime environment. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or dictating development processes, but about choosing a concrete component of the system architecture.

The ADR decides to use Optimistic Concurrency as the concurrency control mechanism in the system, which is a behavioral architectural element affecting how data changes are managed concurrently. This is a decision about creating/selecting a specific architectural element (concurrency control strategy) in the system design, thus fitting the Existence category. It is not about forbidding an element (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting a general quality or constraint (Property), nor about development process or organizational context (Executive).

The ADR primarily decides to create a new client application integrated with the existing MMW system, specifying architectural elements such as repository structure, deployment strategy, and technology stack. This is a decision about the existence and structure of a new software element within the system, fitting the Existence category. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting general system properties or qualities (Property), nor about development process or organizational aspects alone (Executive). Although deployment and repository management are discussed, these serve the purpose of integrating the new client app, which is part of the system to be built, confirming the Existence classification with high confidence.

The decision mandates the inclusion of an integrity check mechanism for assets in the system, effectively creating a behavioral element (integrity check) that affects how assets are processed and included. This is about adding a specific behavior to the system's operation, thus an Existence decision. It is not about forbidding an element (Ban/Non-Existence), nor is it a general quality or constraint (Property), nor about development process or organizational aspects (Executive).

The ADR defines the existence and selection of specific shell options as architectural elements that will be part of the system's design and implementation. It specifies which shells (e.g., cmd, powershell, bash, python) are supported and how they are invoked, thus creating or choosing elements of the system's runtime behavior. This is clearly an Existence decision because it governs what elements (shell interpreters and their invocation templates) will exist in the system. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting general system properties or constraints (Property), nor about development process or organizational decisions (Executive).

The decision is about modifying the ComponentLifecycle interface by adding default implementations to its methods, which changes the structure of this architectural element. This enables new functional interfaces to extend ComponentLifecycle, effectively creating or modifying software elements in the system. It is not about forbidding elements, setting general properties, or governing the development process, but about the existence and structure of an interface and its methods in the system design.

The ADR decides to create and expose a REST API as a structural and behavioral element of the system architecture. It specifies the adoption of REST architectural style constraints, which define how the system components (clients and servers) interact and how services are exposed. This is a clear Existence decision because it establishes the presence of a REST API element in the system design. It is not about forbidding elements (Ban/Non-Existence), nor about setting general quality rules or constraints independent of element existence (Property), nor about development process or organizational aspects (Executive).

The decision is about creating a help subcommand element in the tool that provides usage documentation.
